issues.description: Blocking read with no timeout can hang the parent forever if writer stalls without closing
issues.detail: Once data arrives, you strip O_NONBLOCK and loop on blocking read() with no poll, no timeout, and no process-exit check. If the subprocess wedges mid-write (stuck child, signal-lost, slow producer), the parent hangs indefinitely. The whole point of the original poll loop was liveness. You traded a truncation bug for a hang bug.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler is now dead code with a misleading comment
issues.detail: After switching to blocking mode and entering the inner while-True, BlockingIOError cannot be raised by os.read(). The except branch only ever catches errors from the initial non-blocking read before any data, where 'continue waiting' was already the prior behavior. The pass with 'File not ready yet' comment is misleading — say what it actually handles or delete it.

issues.description: Removed check_process_exited fallback handles a real macOS case the new code doesn't
issues.detail: The deleted branch existed because on some systems poll() returns no events and read() returns empty without EOF when the writer dies abnormally. The new code only enters blocking mode after first data arrives. If the subprocess crashes before writing anything, you fall through to the bottom check — fine — but if it writes a partial buffer then crashes without closing cleanly, blocking read may not return 0. Document or test this path.

issues.description: Outer else branch reduced to bare 'pass' — dead structure
issues.detail: The else: pass with a multi-line comment is noise. Either the outer poll/read loop still has a purpose (waiting for first byte) — in which case say so in two words — or collapse it. Right now the diff leaves a vestigial control structure that the next maintainer has to puzzle over. Smaller, clearer diff.

issues.description: No test added for the race condition being fixed
issues.detail: Bug report cites an intermittent JSONDecodeError at ~86KB. A regression test that writes >64KB (pipe buffer size) across multiple write() calls then closes, with the reader exercising the new path, would lock this in. Without it, the next refactor reintroduces the bug.

issues.description: fcntl flag swap not wrapped — if the inner loop raises, fd is left in blocking mode
issues.detail: Not catastrophic since the fd is local to the function and presumably closed by the caller, but if anything in this module ever reuses the fd or shares it, the mode change leaks. A try/finally around the blocking-mode section is the maintainer-six-years-from-now-friendly version.

review.summary: The diagnosis is correct and the POSIX reasoning about blocking-mode EOF is sound — this is a real race and the fix direction is right. But the implementation trades a truncation bug for a hang bug: once you flip to blocking mode there is no timeout, no liveness check, and no way out if the writer wedges. The BlockingIOError branch becomes dead code, the outer else collapses to a 'pass' with a stale comment, and the macOS fallback that was deleted handled a case the new path doesn't fully cover. NEEDS-WORK: keep the blocking-read insight, but bound it with a deadline or periodic process-exit check, clean up the dead branches, and add a >64KB multi-write regression test before this lands.
